owner_adjudication.inspector_observation_preserved_verbatim: The integrated product collar is rendered in flat mid-brown #705242, which is a warm earth tone with no chromatic relationship to the rose-pink body (#D9BDB5) or the artwork ink (#502525). In the reference concept the collar is a rose-gold metallic band that acts as a chromatic bridge between the pink body and the dark closure. Without that bridging tone the integrated flat version presents a three-colour stack (pink / brown / near-black) where the collar reads as an unrelated intrusion rather than a luxury connector. This is a new integrated-system observation: it only manifests when the flat colour system is read as a complete product stack rather than as isolated accepted swatches.

reason: body, collar and closure are distinct physical components
VQ-2 uses flat concept colours only
VQ-3 will judge frosted glass, metallic collar, closure material, reflections and integrated colour response
the colour separation does not damage hierarchy or brand identity

owner_adjudication.area: Artwork block left-alignment vs bottle centroid — negative-space imbalance on right
owner_adjudication.inspector_observation_preserved_verbatim: The artwork block occupies 80.7% of body width but is left-anchored, leaving approximately 19% of the body width as unoccupied right-side space below the label zone. The divider rule, logo, and both name lines all share the same left datum, producing a deliberate asymmetry that is concept-consistent. However, in the integrated flat view — with no tonal gradient or glass edge to carry the eye — the raw right-side void is visually heavier than in the reference, where frosted-glass curvature and subtle shadow fill the same zone perceptually. The void is not resolved by any graphic device in the flat concept, making it read as incomplete rather than intentional when the product is viewed in isolation (Image 2). This is an integration-level finding: the right-side negative space is acceptable in the reference context but unresolved in the flat integrated product.

reason: the left datum derives from concept #97 and was accepted during VQ-2

owner_adjudication.area: Logo scale relative to hero type block
owner_adjudication.inspector_observation_preserved_verbatim: The logo-to-'Rose'-width ratio is 0.813, meaning the BBROSE logo is only marginally smaller than the width of the 'Rose' line. In the reference concept the logo is visually subordinate because the frosted body and surrounding white space give it breathing room. In the flat integrated product the logo sits in very close proximity above a large negative-space gap before the divider, then an even larger hero type block. The logo therefore reads as weakly anchored — too small to command the upper zone, too large to be a discreet brand mark. The gap between the logo baseline and the divider rule is perceptually disproportionate to the gap between the divider and the 'Rose' headline.

reason: accepted logo/Rose ratio 0.8133 against the measured reference target 0.8134
the previous 0.6035 was explicitly rejected as visually undersized
the inspector's recommendation does not override the reference-derived measurement, the owner-approved VQ-2 composition, or the accepted final-front-artwork state

owner_adjudication.area: Colour coherence — four-tone system chromatic isolation
owner_adjudication.inspector_observation_preserved_verbatim: Viewed as a complete colour system, the four tones split into two unconnected pairs: {#D9BDB5 pink body} and {#705242 brown collar / #493034 dark closure / #502525 artwork ink}. The pink body has no warm-brown undertone relative to the collar, so the body-to-collar junction reads as a colour discontinuity rather than a tone family. In the reference concept rose-gold metallic unifies the warm register across all zones. In the flat system there is no hue shared between the pink body and the brown/dark group, which weakens product-family coherence at the integrated stage.

reason: this is the collar-colour observation restated at system level; the same ruling applies
